$comment: Why this case is in the corpus: the EVIDENCE_GAPS_HEADING branch used to set inGaps and gapsDepth without
touching currentCriterion, so a `### Evidence Gaps` subsection written one level under a domain (the template's
per-domain shape, distinct from the report's single top-level `## Evidence Gaps` section) left whatever criterion
heading was still open. Every line of a domain section feeds citationsIn regardless of label or inGaps state, so a
`**Suggested Evidence:**` bullet inside that nested subsection was read as further evidence for the last criterion
before it, a citation the gap bullet names as MISSING rather than as grounding for anything. Found in the same
review pass as the byStrippedName finding but by a different mechanism: an unrelated section leaking a citation
into a criterion's grounding rather than two headings colliding.
The report is CONSTRUCTED: gapped-correct-audit's report with a `### Evidence Gaps` subsection inserted under
Reliability, right after Disaster Recovery and before the Maintainability domain, carrying one gap bullet
(`**Burn-in dashboard link**`) with a `**Suggested Evidence:** docs/tech-spec.md` line, and nothing else touched.
docs/tech-spec.md is a real file (already cited under Test Coverage and Code Duplication) so it is not fabricated,
and Disaster Recovery is the criterion left open when the nested heading is read.
The fix clears currentCriterion in the EVIDENCE_GAPS_HEADING branch, the same way the domain-heading branch
already clears it: the nested subsection still contributes docs/tech-spec.md to Reliability's domain-level
citations (that reading is unconditional on the label), but with no criterion open it is not pushed into any
criterion's grounding.
Reverting to the version that leaves currentCriterion untouched and replaying this case fails it: groundedCriteria
moves from {17,17} to {16,17} and ungroundedCitations gains `reliability: Disaster Recovery ->
docs/tech-spec.md`, a citation nobody wrote as evidence for Disaster Recovery scoring it ungrounded, which is the
regression this case exists to catch.
derivation: A nested `### Evidence Gaps` subsection was inserted under Reliability, after Disaster Recovery, and nothing else
changed, so every status, count and ceiling below not touching Reliability's own citations or gaps is
Statuses, coverage, thresholds, overall, unknownThreshold and cleanFalsePositives: identical to
gapped-correct-audit, since none of those readers touch Reliability's citations or gap count.
Citations: performance, security and maintainability are identical to gapped-correct-audit. Reliability carries
seven entries where gapped-correct-audit carries six: its original six `evidence/reliability-2026-08.json`
citations, one per criterion, plus `docs/tech-spec.md` from the nested subsection's Suggested Evidence line,
collected because every domain-section line feeds citationsIn regardless of label. docs/tech-spec.md is real
(already cited under Maintainability), so fabricated stays empty.
Grounding: seventeen of the seventeen criteria with declared evidence are grounded, matching gapped-correct-audit
exactly. The nested Evidence Gaps heading clears currentCriterion the same way a domain heading does, so
docs/tech-spec.md is never pushed into Disaster Recovery's (or any criterion's) citation list; it reaches only
Reliability's domain-level citations above. ungroundedCitations stays empty.
Evidence gaps: two, where gapped-correct-audit has one. GAP_ITEM matches the nested subsection's
`**Burn-in dashboard link**` bullet the same way it matches the top-level section's `**Test Coverage**` bullet, so
both are collected in the order they appear in the document.

unknownThreshold.field: a threshold is recorded as UNKNOWN
